title: LLM systems: short summaries + ideas (scratchpad)
content:
Quick context: personal scratchpad for papers/posts I skimmed in late 2025 / early 2026. Mostly tech/system takeaways I want to test in Redwood serving runtime. Lots of shorthand and TODOs — notes to self.

Paper / blog: 'FastKV: compact key-value caches for autoregressive models' (arXiv, 2025) — quick take:
- Core idea: compressed block-level KV snapshots + async / lossy restore when cold-starting sequences. Emphasize low-RAM representation that still retrieves high-quality past tokens for short contexts.
- Why it matters for us: reduces memory pressure on multi-tenant GPUs and makes prewarm faster for tail requests.
- Downsides: potential quality regressions when compression lossy; needs heuristics to decide which KV frames to keep.
- Experiment idea: add a FastKV-style backend to local model runner and measure PPL + latency for 512->2048 continued conversations on 2-3 open models (Llama-3-small/medium analogs).
- Implementation notes: benchmark compression ratios, CPU decompress cost, and potential offload to NVMe (async read).

Paper: 'Dynamic MoE routing for low-latency inference' (NeurIPS 2025 spotlight talk) — notes:
- Main claim: small, conditional routing decisions at runtime can preserve compute while saving FLOPs relative to dense models for many user queries.
- Interesting: routing simplified so each token touches just 1 expert in later layers, with cheap gating.
- Applicability: for Dedicated and Private deployments where customers want lower cost per token but still a high-quality model. Needs hardware-aware kernel and per-batch expert balancing.
- Risk: increased variance in latency due to load-imbalance of experts — SRE headache. Need policy for overflow routing (fallback to dense replica).

Paper: 'Quantization-aware compilation for mixed-precision kernels' (systems workshop paper) — notes:
- Approach: annotate subgraphs where 8-bit is safe vs 4-bit risky, perform per-layer verification with short eval sets to pick quant levels automatically.
- Redwood idea: integrate into Optimize recommendation engine — run small synthetic evals (10–50 examples) during model onboarding to propose quant profiles, not just per-model defaults.
- Quick TODO: prototype using q8->q4 pipeline on toy GPT architecture and measure token-error or BLEU-like metric across quant steps.

Conference notes: ICLR 2026 workshop lightning (observability for generative models) — key ops takeaways:
- Tracing token-level end-to-end latencies is useful but noisy; add aggregation by route/model/account + percentile tracking.
- A few teams used deterministic synthetic prompt suites (100 prompts) to detect regressions post-deploy — low cost and high signal. Could be folded into our rollout checks.

Short paper summary: 'Prefix caching vs KV caching tradeoffs' (forum thread + blog) — my notes:
- Prefix caching (store full softmax outputs / logits for prefix) cheaper on lookup but brittle to sampling randomness / temperature changes; KV caching (store keys/values) is more flexible but heavier.
- Redwood decision: keep KV as primary but expose a hybrid mode in Dedicated where customers can trade-off memory for deterministic replay.
- Action: document where hybrid mode makes sense (RAG vs. chat).

Personal experiments & ideas (ordered rough priority):
1) FastKV PoC: 2-week spike. Goal: 20% reduction in steady-state GPU memory for long chat sessions with <3% quality loss on automated evals. Metrics: memory, tail p99 latency, PPL on test dialogs.
2) Mini MoE simulation: simulate token routing imbalance using our existing batching simulator. Goal: quantify p99 latency increase for 1, 2, 4 experts per request. If p99 > SLA threshold, design overflow to dense fallback.
3) Quantization autotuner: run small calibration per model type during catalog onboarding; store profiles in model metadata and surfacing in Console.

Open questions / things to ask Kai / SRE: 
- How realistic is async NVMe offload for KV restore in our Dedicated fleets? Any prior infra constraints?
- For MoE, do we have telemetry at per-core / per-device queue depth to measure load imbalance? If not, instrument minimal counters.

Notes to self about writing up: keep this doc informal, later copy-clean into a formal RFC if any PoC looks promising. Link experiments to Linear tickets and include dataset/seed details.

Scratch lists / quick checklist:
- [ ] Create Linear ticket for FastKV-PoC (owner: Emily)
- [ ] Add tiny synthetic eval harness (100 prompts) to rollout jobs (owner: Kai)
- [ ] Add quant-profile field to model_catalog schema (owner: eng-platform)

Random references I liked while reading: 
- FastKV repo prototype (conceptual): https://github.com/facebookresearch/fast-kv-cache (bookmark)
- Short thread on prefix vs KV tradeoffs: https://twitter.com/example/thread/1
- NeurIPS talk slides (MoE routing): https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2025/Slides/example.pdf

Final quick reflections: these papers are mostly incremental but push operational levers (compression, routing, small evals) that directly impact cost and latency. For Redwood's thesis (serve economics + reliability) — experiments that measure both quality delta and unit cost are most persuasive. Keep focus on reproducible microbenchmarks and integrate the best candidates into Optimize recommendations rather than shipping radical model changes without ops controls.

-- end of scratchpad (will prune later)
